app_evidence.finding: Dependencies include Supabase, Next, NextAuth, React, and Sentry, but no Redis or Valkey client.
Homepage feed uses Next unstable_cache and existing edge/Supabase fallback data flow.
Public API and page caching is currently CDN/header based.
Contact API anti-abuse is documented as route-level origin validation, Turnstile, and rate limiting.
Redis/KV appears as a future quota guardrail category, not as an active app dependency.

workloads.queue: no concrete backend-owned queue workload identified
workloads.cache: current public caching is Next/CDN/Supabase based
workloads.rate_limiter: no shared backend Redis rate-limiter dependency identified
workloads.session_state: admin auth uses JWT session strategy; no Redis session store identified
workloads.feed_coordination: feed automation is not currently owned by this backend host

future_install_gate.workload_owner: must be a concrete app, worker, or backend issue before install
future_install_gate.network: bind to localhost or a private Docker network only; never expose a Redis or Valkey TCP port publicly
future_install_gate.authentication: require authentication or an equivalent private-network access boundary
future_install_gate.resource_limits: document maxmemory, CPU expectation, and eviction policy before apply
future_install_gate.persistence: cache/rate-limit data should be non-persistent; durable queues need a restore strategy before production use
future_install_gate.backup: only persistent Redis or Valkey data is backed up; rebuildable cache indexes are explicitly excluded
future_install_gate.health_check: define app readiness and degraded behavior before adding a runtime dependency
future_install_gate.observability: collect low-cardinality service health, memory, evictions, connected clients, and persistence errors if installed
future_install_gate.fallback: app behavior must degrade safely when Redis or Valkey is unavailable

validation.live_verification: read-only until a later approved protected apply
